newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Minority interests within the National Empowerment Consortium, which is buying a 35 percent controlling stake in Johnnic worth about four billion rand from Anglo American, are calling for an extension of deadlines to allow smaller groups to raise affordable finance to fund their shares in the deal.

- Paper and packaging group Kohler saw an improvement in attributable earnings in the year to August, boosted by its focus on core packaging and consumer interests developed during the past two years.

- Perskor minorities managed on Sunday to stall the group's purchase of Kagiso Publishers, a move which would give them time to lodge further protests which could permanently derail the deal, analysts said.

- The KwaZulu-Natal legislature's public accounts committee has set up a team of "ghostbusters" to track down an estimated 36,000 non-existent public servants who have been draining the province of about 1.5 billion rand a year.
- The multi-million acquisition of Kagiso Publishers by Perskor has been put on hold and may have to be abandoned following the protest of minorities.
- Three-month Treasury bill rates hit a six-month low of 15.01 percent on Friday as commercial banks prepared for the annual December cash crunch.
- PX, the container transport and consignment division of state-owned Transnet, will relaunch itself by March in an attempt to reverse its disappointing performance.

- Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma will meet members of her ministry and other stakeholders on Monday to hammer out a response to the blistering attack on her over tabacco policy by Rembrandt Group chairman Johann Rupert.
